title: Snapchat and TikTok Ads in the UAE: When They Are Worth It
metaTitle: Snapchat and TikTok Ads in the UAE
description: Snapchat and TikTok ads in the UAE: who each reaches here, what the creative has to look like, how to test one, and when to ignore both.

blocks.v: Most UAE advertising budgets go to Google and Meta, and for most businesses that is correct. Snapchat and TikTok get skipped, usually without being considered, and occasionally that is a mistake worth money.
Here is when each is worth testing, what the creative has to look like, and when to leave both alone.
Snapchat, which is stronger here than elsewhere

Snapchat has a genuinely different position in this region than it does in most markets. It retains a large, young, local audience, and the cost per click is frequently the lowest of any platform available here.

That makes it interesting for consumer products, food and beverage, retail, events and anything with an impulse price point. It makes it poor for anything sold to a business, and poor for a considered purchase that needs several conversations.
The creative has to be vertical, fast and native. An ad that was designed for a feed and cropped for Snapchat will perform like a cropped ad.
TikTok, where the format decides everything

Cheap reach and a real audience, and the hardest platform of the four to use well. The format punishes anything that looks like advertising, which means the Meta creative you already have is almost never the right starting point.

What works is content that would survive without the ad label: someone explaining something, showing something, or demonstrating a result. Produced cheaply and frequently rather than expensively and once.
It works for products with a visual hook. It works badly where somebody must trust a supplier before spending, which is most professional services, including mine.
When to ignore both

v: Your total monthly ad budget is under about AED 5,000. Spread across a third platform it will not leave the learning phase on any of them.
You sell to businesses. LinkedIn and Google are where those decisions get made.
Your product needs explaining before anyone would want it. Short-form video is a poor place to teach.
You cannot produce new creative monthly. Both platforms burn through creative faster than Meta does.

blocks.v: The honest comparison
How to test one properly

v: Pick one, not both. Two underfunded tests produce two unreliable answers.
Budget enough to leave the learning phase, which means a few thousand dirhams a month rather than a few hundred.
Produce creative for the platform rather than resizing what you have. This is the step people skip and it is the step that decides the result.
Run it for at least four weeks. Short-form platforms need volume before the delivery settles.
Judge on cost per qualified enquiry, not on views. Views are the cheapest thing either platform sells.

blocks.v: Frequently asked questions
Is Snapchat still relevant in 2026?

In the UAE specifically, yes, more than its global position suggests. It is a regional anomaly worth knowing about, and it is routinely dismissed by people applying international benchmarks to a local market.
Can I run TikTok ads without making TikTok content?

You can run them. They will underperform. The platform's whole advantage is that native content does not feel like advertising, and an obviously produced advert gives that up while still paying for the placement.
Which should a Dubai consumer brand start with?
Snapchat, usually, for the local audience and the price point. Then Instagram, where people save things for later. TikTok third, and only with somebody who can produce content weekly.
What is a sensible test budget?
Enough to get a trustworthy answer, which in this market is a few thousand dirhams a month for at least a month. Below that you are buying an opinion rather than data.
Published 6 October 2026 by a Dubai-based freelance digital marketer.
